title: Policy-driven analytics mirroring for region-bound tenants (auditable failover + purge controls)
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Summary: Build a policy-driven mirroring layer for usage analytics that guarantees region-bound tenants keep event copies and derived analytics inside approved cloud regions, supports auditable failover, and provides safe cross-region fallback and purge workflows.

Goals: 1) Ensure tenants with region/legal constraints never have production usage data written outside their approved region(s) except via explicit, auditable admin action. 2) Provide an automated, observable mirroring pipeline that writes usage-events and processed artifacts (parquet/metrics snapshots) to region-local storage and analytics stores. 3) Add admin controls in Console for quarantine, cross-region export approvals, and emergency failover with full audit logs. 4) Implement retention/purge gates tied to tenant legal_tag and regulatory_profile metadata.

Scope: console-backend routing + ingestion, stream processing layer (regional mirror), regional storage layout, tenant metadata enrichment, routing policy engine, audit logging and admin console controls. Not in scope: refactoring existing model for non-tenant metrics, or deep changes to billing pipelines (separate follow-up).

Architecture proposal: - Event router (console-backend) tags incoming usage-events with tenant_id and legal metadata (legal_tag, regulatory_profile) from tenant-config service. - Router writes a primary region-local topic (kafka/topic-per-region) with strong region affinity. A parallel mirror writes to regional S3/GCS buckets as parquet using streaming file sink for downstream analytics. - Stream processors (Flink/Beam) run regionally and perform validation, dedup, and derive daily metrics; output stays in the same region. - Global control plane keeps only routing policy decisions (no PII/event payloads) and pushes policy updates to routers via signed policies. - Admin flows: (1) Emergency cross-region export requires multi-approver action in Console and creates an auditable export job that records approver IDs, reason, and TTL. (2) Quarantine toggles route events to a secure vault bucket pending review. - Purge workflow: tenant-level retention is driven by retention_days in tenant metadata; a region-local purge worker validates legal_tag and issues delete operations to storage and cleaned downstream tables; all deletes emit audit events to a region-local audit log.

Privacy & compliance controls: - KMS keys are regional (customer-managed optional) and never moved cross-region by default. - All audit logs include request_id, actor, policy_version, and cryptographic signature for tamper-evidence. - Data that must be kept in-region is never replicated to global analytics clusters unless an explicit export job with approvals is executed.

Observability & SLOs: - Metrics: per-tenant ingestion latency, regional drop rate (routing rejects), mirror lag, purge completion time, and number of policy violations. - Dashboards: per-region/day retention compliance, pending quarantine jobs, pending export approvals. - Alerts: mirror lag > 5m (P0), policy violation spikes > 0.1% of events for a tenant (P1).

Trade-offs considered: - Approach A (single global topic + selective replication) reduces operational overhead but risks accidental cross-region writes when config bugs occur. Rejected for high-risk tenants. - Approach B (region-first routing + local topics + mirror) increases per-region infra but gives stronger hard guarantees and simpler audits. Chosen for this work. - We accept increased cost for dedicated regional storage and processors for high-compliance tenants; propose a tiered model where only tagged tenants trigger region-first resources.

Artifacts and links: - PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALYTICS/Regional+Mirroring+PRD - Design doc (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1RegionalMirrorDesign - Prototype PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4876 - Dashboard mockups: https://figma.com/redwood/console-analytics-residency - Compliance sign-off ticket: COM-88

Next steps: 1) Finalize policy schema (legal_tag, regulatory_profile, allowed_regions, export_requirements) and publish to tenant-config API (owner: Platform API). 2) Implement router changes to enrich events and publish to region topics (owner: console-backend). 3) Stand up regional stream processors and region-local sinks as feature-flagged jobs (owner: analytics-infra). 4) Build Console admin flows (owner: console-frontend) and wire approvals to export jobs (owner: ops).
